summary:
Real age verification behind a provider adapter (addendum §2). AGE_VERIFICATION_PROVIDER selects a labeled sandbox (internal /verify/sandbox page that says in large type it proves nothing, posts HMAC-signed callbacks to the real webhook route, refuses production) or a Yoti Age Verification Service adapter (create session → hosted URL, RSA-PSS-signed notifications, result fetch; written from the public docs, UNVERIFIED). src/server/age/service.ts: requirementFor() (jurisdiction stored at signup / refreshed at login, else request geo headers; required when in AGE_VERIFICATION_REGIONS or the defaults; fail-closed switch for unknown locations; verified past AGE_VERIFICATION_VALID_DAYS reads as expired), startVerification(), handleCallback()/applyResult() (signature check, replay rejection, row + user update, audit with actor null and provider ref), viewerAccessFor(). gate.ts throws HttpError(451, age_verification_required, { verifyPath, status, jurisdiction }); the old AGE_ASSURANCE_STRICT_REGIONS path is folded into the same rules. Discovery queries now take a Viewer and withhold media URLs server-side for viewers who still need a check (cards, template page, creator pages, rails, /api/templates), with a placeholder. Settings gains an age-verification card; GET /api/me and settingsFor carry the status. ApiError exposes verifyPath/apiErrorAction for 451. 21 new tests; all 100 pass; typecheck and lint clean.

IMPORTANT for merging: the worktree was created on d2d6cad (the Copilot prototype on main), not the Next.js build, so I reset my branch to claude/playbox-2-foundation-q7fpbs (9e1db60) before working. Both commits sit directly on top of 9e1db60.

unverified: Yoti adapter (src/server/age/providers/yoti.ts): never run against the live service; no account or credentials exist. Written from https://developers.yoti.com/age-verification pages read on 2026-10-12 via WebFetch summaries (direct curl to developers.yoti.com is blocked by the egress proxy). Endpoints and fields relied on: POST {AGE_VERIFICATION_API_URL}/api/v1/sessions with headers Authorization: Bearer <API key>, Yoti-SDK-Id: <SDK ID>, Content-Type: application/json; body type:'OVER', ttl:1800, reference_id (our age_verifications row id), callback {url, auto:true}, cancel_url, synchronous_checks:true, notification_url (only when APP_URL is https), age_estimation {allowed, threshold:25, level:'PASSIVE', authenticity:'AUTO'}, doc_scan {allowed, threshold:18, level:'PASSIVE', authenticity:'AUTO'}, digital_id {allowed, threshold:18}, credit_card/mobile {allowed:false}; response {id, expires_at, status}. Hosted page https://age.yoti.com?sessionId=<id>&sdkId=<SDK ID>; Yoti redirects to callback.url with sessionId appended (handled by GET /api/age-verification/return, which fetches the result). GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/result → {status in PENDING|IN_PROGRESS|PROCESSING|COMPLETE|FAIL|ERROR|CANCELLED|EXPIRED, method}. Notifications: POST JSON {method, state, session_key, reference_id, id, timestamp, evidence_id, sequence_number, signature}; signature = RSA-PSS/SHA-256 over the payload minus sequence_number and signature, serialized with all whitespace removed, salt length = signature bytes − 32 − 2, against Yoti's published Age Verification public key (the docs page shows the PEM; the fetch tool could not reproduce it verbatim, so it is an env var the operator pastes). The signature scheme itself is unit-tested with a locally generated key pair only.
The facial age estimation threshold of 25 (buffer above the legal 18, so borderline faces fall through to a document check) is my reading of Ofcom/Yoti guidance, not confirmed with Yoti.

AGE_VERIFICATION_FAIL_CLOSED=true behaviour is covered by the pure rule (jurisdictionRequired) but not by an integration test, because env() is cached per process and the vitest config fixes the environment.
The sandbox page UI (/verify/sandbox) and the Settings card were typechecked and linted, not rendered in a browser (no next build / e2e run, per the rules).

Yoti's actual retention and privacy terms per method were not read in full (the data-privacy page only states that the relying party gets the result and no directly identifiable information); the privacy policy at yoti.com/privacy/age-verification/ should be cited in the docs.

docsNotes: JURISDICTION RULES. A person's jurisdiction is the code stored on the account (captured from the geo headers at signup, refreshed at every sign-in when a header is present; a missing header keeps the stored value), else the current request's geo headers; anonymous visitors use the headers only. Codes are "GB" or "US-TX" (jurisdictionCode in src/config/jurisdictions.ts). Verification is required when AGE_VERIFICATION_ENFORCE=true and the code falls under AGE_VERIFICATION_REGIONS (comma-separated; a bare "US" covers every state) or, when unset, DEFAULT_AGE_VERIFICATION_REGIONS (GB plus 25 US state codes), plus anything in the older AGE_ASSURANCE_STRICT_REGIONS, which is now folded into the same rule set (the separate "age_assurance_required" 451 is gone; ageAssuranceBlocksRegion remains only as a pure helper). Unknown location with rules configured: AGE_VERIFICATION_FAIL_CLOSED (default false = allowed). HONESTY CAVEAT: the state list was compiled from the Free Speech Coalition tracker as read on 2026-10-12; it is configuration, not legal advice, laws keep changing, and the operator must re-check it before launch and override it with AGE_VERIFICATION_REGIONS. Note also that the geo headers are only as trustworthy as the edge that sets them; a client-supplied header is honoured unless the edge overwrites it. WHAT IS BLOCKED: createDraft/derive (all generation), POST /api/uploads, and explicit media: every public template is treated as explicit on an adults-only site (there is no per-template explicit flag), so a viewer who still needs a check gets cards, rails, the template page, creator pages and /api/templates with no media URL at all (posterUrl/previewUrl null, mediaWithheld true) and a placeholder "Verify your age to see previews" / "Sign in and verify to see previews"; titles, creators and metadata stay. The decision is made once per request by viewerAccess() (src/server/age/access.ts). A user's own Library/creations are not gated (they could not have been made without passing the gate). ERROR SHAPE: HttpError 451 code age_verification_required, message "Your region requires an age check before you can create or upload. It takes a minute.", details { verifyPath: "/settings#age-verification", status, jurisdiction }; src/lib/api.ts appends "Open Settings › Age verification to do it." to the message and exposes ApiError.verifyPath / apiErrorAction(err) for a toast link (create-panel.tsx was not edited). STATUSES per user: unverified, pending, verified, failed, expired (expired is computed, not stored: verified with age_verified_at older than AGE_VERIFICATION_VALID_DAYS, default 365, reads as expired and must be redone; changing VALID_DAYS changes existing users' expiry; age_verifications.expires_at records what was valid at completion). A verified account is never downgraded by a later failed attempt; a user who is verified and not expired cannot start another check (409 already_verified). ROUTES: POST /api/age-verification/start (signed-in, rate limit 10/h/user, returns { url, provider, sandbox, verificationId }); POST /api/webhooks/age-verification/[provider] (raw body, must be the active provider, signature checked before anything is read, unsigned → 400 callback_unsigned, forged → 400 callback_bad_signature, malformed → 400, unknown reference → 404, already completed → 409 callback_replayed, pending outcomes change nothing; exempt from the origin check like other webhooks); GET /api/age-verification/return (the provider's redirect target; for the signed-in owner of the pending check it fetches the result from the provider's API and applies it; the redirect itself never changes a status); GET /api/me and settingsFor() include ageVerification { status, jurisdiction, required, verifiedAt, expiresAt, verifyPath, provider {key,label,sandbox,configured,methods,validDays,enforce}, history[] }. ageVerificationStatus() in src/server/age/index.ts is the health/report summary (no secrets). AUDIT: age_verification.pending (actor = the user), age_verification.verified / age_verification.failed (actor null), target age_verification/<row id>, metadata { provider, providerRef, userId, jurisdiction, method, expiresAt | reason }. DATA STORED: users.age_verification_status/age_verified_at/age_verification_provider/jurisdiction; age_verifications rows (provider, status, provider_ref, method, jurisdiction, failure_reason, started_at, completed_at, expires_at). NOT STORED: ID images, documents, selfies, biometrics, estimated age, names or dates of birth from the provider; the Yoti adapter requests none of it (Yoti returns only the over/under outcome) and nothing from the callback body is persisted beyond the reference, method and reason. Logs record provider, reference and rejection reason only. RETENTION: verification rows are kept with the account (they are the compliance record) and cascade-delete with the user row; deleteAccount leaves them in place like consent records. SANDBOX: AGE_VERIFICATION_PROVIDER=sandbox sends the user to /verify/sandbox?ref=… (signed-in owner of the pending row only; 404 in production or when another provider is active), which is labeled "Sandbox" in demo tone and states it proves nothing; its two buttons deliver server-pre-signed HMAC-SHA256 bodies (header x-hushloom-sandbox-signature, secret AGE_VERIFICATION_WEBHOOK_SECRET or a dev-only fallback) to the real webhook route. env() refuses to boot production with the sandbox while AGE_VERIFICATION_ENFORCE=true. YOTI: methods enabled are facial age estimation (threshold 25 as a buffer), identity document scan with liveness/authenticity (threshold 18) and Digital ID (threshold 18); Yoti's own sandbox environment exists but was not integrated. Everything Yoti-specific is UNVERIFIED (see the unverified list) and the public key must be pasted by the operator. UI: Settings card src/components/age-verification-card.tsx with id="age-verification" (status badge, detected jurisdiction, what it means, provider with sandbox label, Verify now / Continue / Verify again, attempt history); it is mounted in settings.tsx with one import line and one JSX line and reads data.ageVerification structurally so the Settings type did not change. The /policies "Adults only" paragraph now describes the real check.

Discovery signatures changed (browseTemplates/cardsByIds/similarTemplates/forYou/recentlyViewed/followingFeed take a Viewer {id, explicitAllowed}; creatorPage/creatorAnalytics likewise). Any other track calling these must pass a Viewer; tests/integration/platform.test.ts was updated at its two forYou() call sites.

Should a verified-but-expired account also be written back as 'expired' (currently computed on read), and should the stored jurisdiction ever be overridden by a stricter current-request header? I followed the brief (stored wins) and noted the VPN-at-login caveat.
Whether the operator wants a per-template explicit flag so some posters could be shown to unverified viewers; today every public template is treated as explicit.
The Yoti age-estimation threshold (25) and the choice of Yoti's Age Verification Service (age.yoti.com) over its Identity Verification API should be confirmed with Yoti/legal before go-live.
